Introduction

Sik-K, born Kwon Min-sik, is a prominent rapper, singer, and songwriter best known for his melodic & versatile sound that blends hip-hop, trap, and R&B. He first came into the spotlight as a contestant on Show Me the Money 4 in 2015, where he joined Team AOMG (Jay Park and Loco) and reached the Top 16. This appearance boosted his visibility in the Korean hip-hop scene. In 2016, he made his official debut with the EP FLIP, released under the independent crew OTC (Outside the Circle). In 2017, he signed with H1GHR MUSIC, a label founded by Jay Park and Cha Cha Malone to bridge Korean and American hip-hop artists.

Beyond his solo ventures, Sik-K is a member of the influential hip-hop collective Yelows Mob, which includes producers and artists such as GroovyRoom, Mac Kidd, Boycold, and Vangdale, who are frequent collaborators. He released his first full-length album FL1P (2019), followed by HEADLINER (2020) before enlisting for mandatory military service.
Fans of Sik-K often praise his production choices and emotional openness. Fan favorite tracks include “Fire,” “HALF,” and "Ring Ring”.

After completing his military service and fulfilling his contract with H1GHR MUSIC, Sik-K left the label in 2022 and established his own company, KC (Kwon Min-sik Company) the following year, where he currently serves as CEO.

In April 2025, Sik-K was sentenced to a two-year suspension, probation, and 40 hours of drug prevention education after voluntarily surrendering for multiple drug offenses. His swift return to performing—resuming festival appearances just 48 hours after sentencing—sparked controversy. Public opinion was divided, with some criticizing his actions while others acknowledged his remorse and voluntary surrender.

Despite the controversy, Sik-K received major recognition at the 2025 Korean Hip-Hop Awards. He won Artist of the Year, KC won Label of the Year, HAON and Sik-K took Music Video of the Year for “KC (BUST IT DOWN),” and Vangdale earned Producer of the Year. The same year, Sik-K released K-Flip+, a deluxe version of his collaborative EP with Lil Moshpit. The album samples traditional Korean sounds from artists of various genres like Silica Gel (indie rock), Kim Sawol (folk indie), Epik High, Dok2, The Koxx, Verbal Jint, and Jay Park (hip-hop), bridging old and new influences.
